All historical evidence rows retain their exact old identities; they do not qualify this changed source. UTF-8 string range now has an explicit source implementation and separate CI-only unrun acceptance record; its retired non-array-range diagnostic originals are preserved as positive same-input obligations. No old evidence was renewed. Nil-only predeclared error local values now have a separate source-bound implementation and UNRUN acceptance record. General interface/runtime support and original math/bits acceptance remain unimplemented; no historical evidence is renewed. Basic-interface declarations and method-set/shared-value plans now have independent source-bound implementation rows and CI-only UNRUN acceptance. Declaration/native nil-only obligations are distinct from dynamic-interface reference-only originals; no runtime or project qualification is claimed. Struct tags on the admitted value-record domain now have explicit source implementation and CI-only UNRUN acceptance; historical diagnostic originals are retained as positive same-input obligations, not relabeled evidence. Labels/goto now have a separate source implementation and CI-only UNRUN acceptance; the full fixed official label.go is retained unchanged. No historical evidence or original math/bits result is renewed. Rune literals and untyped rune defaults now have a separate source-bound implementation and UNRUN acceptance. Exact upstream character literal inputs retain their os-dependency or invalid-Unicode boundary; no old evidence is renewed. No historical execution evidence or real math/bits acceptance is renewed. Blank package types now have complete checked declarations without name registration, with source-bound UNRUN acceptance. Complete official issue8079 stays unchanged; no historical execution or whole math/bits evidence is renewed. Static blank imports now check complete static source graphs without name binding. features.title: Scalar and static-string expression switches
features.scope: Optional init and selector; integer/defined-integer/bool/static-string equality; left-to-right case evaluation; selector snapshot; delayed default; independent clause scopes; explicit fallthrough; loop continue versus switch break; syntactic return termination. This historical scalar-switch scope does not qualify type switches, interfaces, aggregate equality or labels/goto; separate feature rows track later source work. Complete original switches_valid.go is preserved; old invalid switches.go remains a same-source PCC/official negative.

features.title: Value-array range and array len/cap
features.scope: Fixed value arrays only; zero/one/two iteration variables; snapshot when elements are consumed; range expression call evaluation and constant len/cap omission; typed int indices and builtin results; two-phase target assignment; hidden induction index; named scalar element identity; loop/switch break and continue. Pointer arrays, slices, strings/runes, integer/map/channel/function range and closure-observable iteration-variable identities remain outside this runtime-qualified subset.

features.title: Integer range with typed one-time bounds
features.scope: Qualified bounded Linux pcc0/self integer range: zero/one iteration variable, all admitted signed/unsigned and defined integer types, contextual untyped bounds, one-time bound evaluation, per-iteration assignment targets, hidden width-correct induction, zero/negative limits and structured control flow. Addresses of range-declared variables remain explicitly unimplemented; no closure/heap/panic/native-pcc1/Mac/complete-Go claim.

features.title: Dynamic division panics and runtime error panic operands
features.scope: Linux targets: a dynamic divisor is checked after both operands are evaluated; zero causes the uncaught terminal panic of runtime.divideError (report 'panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero', status 2), and signed MIN / -1 == MIN, MIN % -1 == 0 without reaching a trapping machine division. The whole operand of panic may be a runtime-owned error bound by //go:linkname (runtime.divideError, runtime.overflowError); the panic reports its runtime/panic.go Error() text without materializing an interface value. Only the admitted no-defer/no-recover/no-goroutine domain reaches this terminal panic. Other value uses of runtime-owned errors stay go.unsupported.interface-types; non-Linux targets reach the go.unsupported.builtin-io target boundary. The unchanged math/bits normal production files now all lower to IR (previously bits.go:507:9); upstream tests remain unrun. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Dot imports
features.scope: Source implementation with authored, execution-unrun obligations for file-block dot imports of exported declarations from supplied original source packages. Lookup retains dependency-owned types, symbols, methods and generic instances; disjoint imports, collisions, local shadowing, per-file use and isolation are checked without a package-block copy. The exact old import-only diagnostic source remains a missing-source or unused-import error, not a positive program. The unchanged math/bits test file reaches a later syntax boundary; runtime/interface/linkname/dynamic-initialization and whole-project acceptance remain open. No historical evidence is renewed.

features.title: Deferred calls
features.scope: Explicitly rejected capability: defer statements. `defer Call` parses (a parenthesized or non-call operand is a syntax error at the position gc reports) and the deferred call is checked as an expression statement would be (conversions and undefined functions are ordinary errors), but running deferred calls at function exit, also while panicking, and recover() need the shared unwinding design; terminal panics assume no deferred call exists, so the checker rejects the statement. No broader implementation or runtime support is claimed.

features.title: Function values
features.scope: Explicitly rejected capability: function values. Function types and function literals (including a called literal used as a statement) are parsed and retained, but closures, captured-variable storage and indirect calls are not implemented, so the checker rejects the first function type or literal it checks. No broader implementation or runtime support is claimed.

features.title: Owned runtime package surface
features.scope: Explicitly rejected capability: names of the owned runtime package that are not implemented yet. Package runtime is runtime-coupled and owned by the compiler; when no source is supplied for it, imports bind PCC's owned package, which implements the Error interface (interface { error; RuntimeError() }, the runtime/error.go contract). Every other exported name (GOOS, GC, ...) is rejected with this code; unexported names and unused imports stay ordinary errors. No broader runtime support is claimed.

features.title: Direct non-retaining pointer receiver methods
features.scope: Qualified bounded Linux pcc0/self implementation: concrete local defined types and aliases, direct p.M and addressable x.M calls, direct (*T).M expressions, ordinary nullable pointer ABI and closed non-retaining source call graph. Nil-safe bodies work without caller-derived nonnull; unproven dereference, method values, interfaces, pointer results and escaping storage remain explicit frontiers. No runtime/backend/GC or full Go claim. Acceptance: 23 full-width native observations, complete main, five exact graduated originals and one two-package same-input comparison; 15 normal invalid-source rejections and ten valid-but-unsupported build-only controls remain distinct.

features.title: Local pointer escape
features.scope: Escaping local aliases that outlive their lexical pointee region remain unsupported; same-or-inner-region aliases and call-duration parameter provenance are implemented separately. A nil guard does not extend pointee lifetime.

features.title: Escaping pointer results and unchecked call contracts
features.scope: Pointer-valued returns and unchecked/retaining callees remain unsupported. Independently source-guarded direct parameters are implemented only for a verified complete non-retaining supplied-source call closure; no caller-derived nonnull assumptions.

features.title: Pointer-bearing storage
features.scope: Package pointer storage, pointer-bearing aggregates and pointer-to-pointer storage require recursive ownership/lifetime analysis.

features.title: Unproven evaluated pointer indirection
features.scope: Evaluated indirection without a source-control-flow nonnil proof requires an unimplemented shared-runtime nil-panic path. Nullable storage itself is implemented. Unevaluated operands and existing control edges do not invent a dereference obligation or erase one that executes.

features.title: Per-iteration pointer identity
features.scope: Taking addresses of declared for/range iteration bindings requires distinct per-iteration storage; entry-slot reuse is not accepted as Go identity. The same boundary covers addressed local declarations reentered by a backward goto; no reused entry slot is an identity proof.

features.title: Addressed composite literal allocation
features.scope: Addressed composite literals require distinct allocation/lifetime analysis rather than reusing a value temporary.

features.title: Live pointer-to-fixed-array range
features.scope: Qualified bounded Linux pcc0/self implementation: admitted *[N]E and defined/alias types, constant-length index-only non-evaluation, nullable zero-length iteration, source-guarded nonempty element access, once-captured pointer with live element loads and ordinary iteration assignments. No slice allocation/shared-runtime/backend/GC or complete Go claim. features.title: Scalar bootstrap output and terminal uncaught panic
features.scope: Implemented and executed in bounded Linux pcc0/self domain: Linux print/println of admitted fixed-width integer, boolean and immutable-backed string values, capturing arguments once before output; actual terminal uncaught panic with scalar payload reporting and no normal CFG successor. This only applies to the admitted no-defer/no-recover/no-goroutine/no-foreign-callback domain. Full panic/unwind/recovery, general interface payloads and non-Linux output are not implemented. Existing owned IR/syscall primitives are reused without allocator, backend or shared runtime edits. Unchanged official ken/for.go and helloworld.go remain the project milestones; authored triggered-panic comparisons retain implementation-specific stderr differences. Writer uses per-thread SIGPIPE block/pending/drain/restore without changing process-wide disposition; broken-stderr real executions and restored-state observers executed successfully. Named-scalar and multiline panic report differences remain explicit. Actual acceptance: unchanged official five-source shard passed (three native/reference executions, one compile-only, one normal source rejection);16 triggered panic status/payload comparisons and five native signal-state observers passed. All16 complete panic reports differ from official Go, retained without normalization. The legacy combined status remains missing/partial rather than claiming raw-report-equivalent terminal panic; exact scalar-output pair is separately qualified. No full Go, standard library, native pcc1, unwind or GC claim.

features.title: Remaining builtin output and panic payload/target domains
features.scope: Explicit unsupported boundaries: non-scalar/nil panic payloads, pointer or other non-scalar bootstrap output, and targets without this owned Linux output/termination path, including the dynamic division-by-zero panic. No general interface ownership, recovery/unwind or platform-runtime behavior is invented. Qualifying value Error() string/String() string panic callbacks are not silently omitted; they require shared interface/runtime support.

features.title: Object-symbol linkname ownership
features.scope: Recognized //go:linkname directives are admitted only in files that import unsafe and must name a declared package function or variable; both violations are normal diagnostics. A variable with no initializer and the predeclared error type binds an owned runtime error value (runtime.divideError, runtime.overflowError), which then reaches the package interface storage boundary. The one-name form, //go:linknamestd, function aliases, other targets and differently typed variables require owned object-symbol binding and runtime ownership. Keyword-plus-ASCII-space recognition and Unicode White_Space argument splitting follow pinned Go 1.27.3 source. Nonblank line-prefix placement is checked first for every //go: directive, excluding only the already-consumed file-initial BOM. Misplacement and malformed arity are normal diagnostics; the capability boundary does not certify the validity of the remaining source.

features.title: Package variables bound to runtime-owned error values
features.scope: A package variable of the predeclared error type bound by //go:linkname to runtime.divideError or runtime.overflowError is a reference to runtime-owned storage: the package emits no global, no initializer and no symbol use for it. Every value use other than the whole operand of a terminal panic (go.capability.division-panic), including comparison and assignment, remains go.unsupported.interface-types until the owned runtime provides the boxed error objects and interface values. The unchanged math/bits package moved from bits_errors.go:12:5 to bits.go:507:9 at this boundary. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Package unsafe operations
features.scope: unsafe is a compiler-owned pseudo-package and never supplied source. A blank import, which //go:linkname requires, introduces no names. A named or dot import, and therefore every unsafe operation, requires pointer and layout semantics that are not implemented.
